{{< include _extensions/live/_knitr.qmd >}}

Every code box on these pages runs real R, inside your browser. There's nothing to install. Edit the code, press **Run Code**, and use **Show Hint** and **Show Solution** when you're stuck. Your edits are saved in this browser, so you can come back later.

## The course

A 10-part progression (an R primer, eight substantive modules and a capstone), each about a week at 3–5 hours. The examples use built-in or package datasets plus one included CSV, so everything is reproducible.

::: {.estimand}
**Applied wet-lab track.** A running western blot case study is threaded through the course using `data/western_blot_example.csv` (WT / HET / KO / RESCUE, 4 biological reps × 3 technical reps each): tidying in Module 1, the ANOVA deep dive in Module 3, assumption checks in Module 5, and a mixed-model treatment of the technical replicates in Module 8.
:::

## Modules

| | Module | Try it |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | [R syntax primer](M0.qmd) | Subsetting, factors, formulas and pipes warm-ups |
| 1 | [R foundations](M1.qmd) | Penguin plot builder; spreadsheet → tidy blot data |
| 2 | [Distributions and simulation](M2.qmd) | CLT explorer and a Student-vs-Welch Type I error simulator |
| 3 | [Classical inference](M3.qmd) | Technical-replicate pseudoreplication simulator; blot ANOVA + post-hocs |
| 4 | [Linear regression](M4.qmd) | Watch the `wt` slope change as you adjust for other predictors |
| 5 | [Regression diagnostics](M5.qmd) | Drag one point around and watch leverage and Cook's distance |
| 6 | [The GLM framework](M6.qmd) | Link-function explorer: link scale vs response scale |
| 7 | [Logistic regression](M7.qmd) | Threshold and cost explorer with a live confusion matrix and ROC |
| 8 | [Count GLMs and mixed models](M8.qmd) | Overdispersion simulator: Poisson vs quasi-Poisson vs negative binomial |
| 9 | [Capstone](M9.qmd) | Analysis templates and a separation simulation sandbox |

The full written notes, mini-projects and reflections live in the Obsidian `.md` files in this repository; these pages cover the hands-on part.

## How to work through this

1. Read the module note (or the summary at the top of each page).
2. Work each exercise in the browser. Get to a stopping point on your own before opening the solution: a wrong answer you can articulate is more useful than a correct one you copied.
3. Do the mini-project in the page's sandbox, or locally in a `.qmd` file.
4. Write 3–5 sentences in the reflection section of the module note.

## Datasets used

- `mtcars`, `iris`, `sleep`, `HairEyeColor`, `warpbreaks`, `ToothGrowth` (base R)
- `palmerpenguins::penguins`
- `MASS::quine`
- `ISLR2::Default`
- `ggplot2::diamonds`
- `lme4::cbpp`
- `data/western_blot_example.csv` (simulated densitometry)

## Tips

- Pages load R once; the first visit is slow, later ones are faster.
- **Start Over** on any box restores the original code.
- Heavy boxes (bootstraps, simulations) can take 10–60 seconds. The button shows a spinner while R works.
- Works best in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop. It runs on phones too, just more slowly.
- To work locally instead, install the packages once:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "tidyverse", "broom", "car", "MASS",
  "palmerpenguins", "ISLR2", "readxl",
  "performance", "emmeans", "DHARMa", "lme4", "lmerTest",
  "pROC", "logistf", "multcomp", "sandwich", "lmtest",
  "ggpubr", "betareg", "glmnet"
))
```
